entries.lesson_title: Periodic Signals as Sums of Sinusoids
entries.core_move: Interpret a periodic continuous-time signal as a weighted sum of sinusoidal harmonic components organized around a fundamental frequency.
Compute the DC component of a periodic signal as its average value over one period and interpret it as the zero-frequency term in a Fourier series.
Compute the Fourier-series fundamental frequency $\omega_0 = 2\pi/T_0$ from a periodic signal's period and use it as the spacing between harmonic components.
Compute harmonic frequencies as integer multiples of the fundamental frequency and interpret each multiple as a sinusoidal component in the Fourier-series frequency-domain view.
Identify sine and cosine waves at integer multiples of the fundamental frequency as basis functions whose weighted combination represents a periodic signal.

Translate a periodic signal between its time-domain waveform and frequency-domain harmonic description by identifying how DC, fundamental frequency, harmonic frequencies, and sine/cosine basis components encode the same signal.
